formula: popular ~ sex + extrav + texp + extrav:texp + (extrav | class)
notes: Hox, Moerbeek & van de Schoot (2018) ch.2, pupils in classes; the running random-slope example with cross-level interaction extrav x texp. popteach is the teacher-rated popularity (alternate response); Z*/C* are standardised/centred copies.

formula: stress ~ age + gender + experien + wardtype + hospsize + expcon + (1 | hospital) + (1 | hospital:ward)
notes: Hox et al. (2018) ch.2/ch.10 three-level model, nurses within wards within hospitals; expcon is the ward-level experimental condition. wardid is the unique ward id (= hospital:ward), ignored as redundant. RULE GAP: the SPSS value labels for 'age' collide (labelled 'male/female' while the column holds numeric ages 23-60); the merge may read 'age' as a category. Z*/C* are standardised/centred copies.

formula: gpa ~ occas + job + sex + highgpa + (occas | student)
notes: Hox et al. (2018) ch.5 longitudinal growth of GPA over six semesters per student; job is the time-varying work hours. admitted (university admission) is a student-level binary alternate outcome, ignored.

formula: REPEAT ~ SEX + PPED + MSESC + (1 | SCHOOLID)
notes: Hox et al. (2018) ch.6 logistic multilevel model; REPEAT (repeated a class) binary, pupils in Thai schools, MSESC the school-mean SES.

formula: estrmeas ~ 1 + (1 | subject)
notes: Hox et al. (2018) ch.9 measurement-reliability / variance-components (ICC) model: 16 repeated estrone assays per subject, empty model. log_estr is the log10 transform (alternate response). estrone.sav is the wide twin.

formula: response ~ mode + year + saliency + (1 | source)
notes: Hox et al. (2018) ch.11 multilevel meta-analysis of survey response rates: data-collection modes (ftf/tel/mail) nested within publication 'source'. respisrr marks whether 'response' holds the rr or cr; cr/rr are the raw rates, denom* the sample sizes (weights), mode dummies derived from mode.

formula: LOR ~ condition + Smoke + Adj + Age + (1 | ID)
notes: Hox et al. (2018) ch.11 bivariate/multivariate meta-analysis: logged odds ratios of asthma and lower-respiratory-disease vs ETS exposure, weighted by inverse variance. RULE GAP: a study-level effect-size table; study 'ID' repeats for only 8 of 59 studies (both conditions), so the grouping is overwhelmingly singleton. Kept per the #24 cluster-repeats rule, but a near-degenerate meta-analysis grouping -- flag for Alex. AstLrdWide.sav is the wide twin. OddsRat raw OR, SE/Var/InvLorW the weights, AstLrd/LrdAst duplicate condition codings.

formula: anti ~ occasion + kidgen + momage + homecog + homeemo + read + (occasion | id)
notes: Hox et al. (2018) longitudinal growth of antisocial behaviour (Curran data), children over occasions; read (reading ability) is the time-varying covariate. kidage6/sq/c, kidagetv and occasion2 are centred/polynomial derived terms.

formula: seizure ~ treat + visit + lbas + lage + (1 | subject)
notes: Hox et al. (2018) Poisson multilevel model, Thall & Vail progabide epilepsy trial, seizure counts over visits per subject. lseiz is log(seizure) (transformed response), v1-v4 the visit dummies derived from visit.

formula: wordlist ~ 1 + (1 | family)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: the help page carries no labels. Six exchangeable IQ subtests (wordlist, cards, matrices, figures, animals, occupats) per child within family; filed as a variance-components model of one subtest with family as grouping (children within families). A multivariate measurement table loaded wide; the other five subtests are alternate responses, ignored. One row filed (no documented model, rule-4).

formula: event ~ period + partrans + pas + (1 | person)
notes: Hox et al. (2018) ch.13 discrete-time survival in person-period form (Capaldi first-sex data): event (had sex) as the hazard, grade as time, parental transition and antisocial behaviour as covariates. grade7-12 are the time dummies, t1-t3 the polynomial time, censored the censoring indicator.

formula: galo ~ sex + feduc + meduc + focc + denom + (1 | school)
notes: Hox et al. (2018) GALO educational data, pupils in schools; galo achievement test as response, parental education/occupation as covariates. The study's own outcome is the ordinal teacher 'advice' (secondary-school recommendation), filed here as an alternate response and ignored because its SPSS coding mixes numeric codes with lowest/highest labels. nmis = count of missing.

formula: respons ~ mode + varlevel + year + saliency + (1 | source)
notes: Hox et al. (2018) ch.11 multivariate multilevel meta-analysis: two outcomes per study (completion rate and response rate, indexed by varlevel) over data-collection modes within 'source'. comp/resp indicate varlevel, mode dummies derived from mode, denom the sample size.

formula: unsafe ~ age + sex + economic + crowded + (1 | street)
notes: Hox et al. (2018) ordinal (proportional-odds) multilevel model; perceived unsafety (never/sometimes/often) of respondents within streets. agediv10/age10c/sexc/econc/crowdedc are rescaled/centred derived copies.

formula: Surv(lengthm, divorce) ~ status + educlev + gender + birthyr + famsize + kid + fastat + moedyrs + faedyrs + mothdiv + (1 | famid)
notes: Hox et al. (2018) ch.13 multilevel survival / shared-frailty model of divorce, siblings within families; lengthm = marriage length (survival time), divorce = event. RULE GAP: survival outcome filed as continuous with the event indicator divorce in ignore (the #22 kidney convention). lengthc is the discretised time, sibdivpr a leave-one-out sibling summary, period53 a derived period column.

formula: rating ~ sexsend + agesend + sexrec + agerec + grsize + (1 | group) + (1 | group:sender) + (1 | group:receiver)
notes: Hox et al. (2018) social-relations / round-robin model: sociometric ratings of each receiver by each sender within a group; sender and receiver crossed within group. Grouping inferred from column names. rating is a 1-7 scale (filed ordinal per the #23 seven-point-rating rule). socscors.sav is the wide twin.

formula: item1 ~ dirsex + pupsex + (1 | school)
notes: Hox et al. (2018) multilevel measurement battery: six Likert items (1-4, low..high) rating the school manager, pupils within schools. The six items are the multivariate responses (multivariate rule, items 4-6 beyond the cap: item4;item5;item6). Grouping school; item coding mixes numeric and low/high labels, model inferred.

formula: item2 ~ dirsex + pupsex + (1 | school)
notes: Hox et al. (2018) school-manager Likert battery, multivariate row 2 (see item1 row).

formula: item3 ~ dirsex + pupsex + (1 | school)
notes: Hox et al. (2018) school-manager Likert battery, multivariate row 3 (see item1 row).

formula: achiev ~ pupsex + pupses + pdenom + sdenom + (1 | pschool) + (1 | sschool)
notes: Hox et al. (2018) cross-classified model: pupils cross-classified by primary school (pschool) and secondary school (sschool), achievement in secondary school as response.

Snijders & Bosker (2012) Table 3.2 (p.28, examples 3.5-3.6), used to illustrate within- and between-group regression; j is the group, i the within-group index. RULE GAP: a 10-row artificial didactic table; the rendered help does not state it is simulated, so it is not excluded, but Tables 3.1/3.2 are textbook constructs -- flag for Alex.

formula: langpost ~ iq_verb + ses + minority + (1 | school)
notes: Snijders & Bosker (2012) example 3.7 (Brandsma data, n=3762), clustering of pupil outcomes in schools; this extract carries both the language (langpost) and arithmetic (aritpost) post-tests, filed as a two-response multivariate pair (the richer modelling uses sheet 04).

formula: aritpost ~ iq_verb + ses + minority + (1 | school)
notes: Snijders & Bosker (2012) Brandsma n=3762, arithmetic post-test, multivariate row 2 (see model_index 1).

formula: langpost ~ iq_verb + ses + female + minority + denomina + sch_ses + sch_iqv + sch_min + (iq_verb | school)
notes: Snijders & Bosker (2012) ch.4-5 running example (Brandsma data, n=3758): random-intercept and random-slope hierarchical linear model of language post-test, iq_verb random over schools, with pupil- and school-level (sch_*) covariates.

formula: langpost ~ langpre + iq_verb + ses + minority + homework + (1 | school)
notes: Snijders & Bosker (2012) ch.9 missing-data chapter (Brandsma n=4016): language post-test on pretest and background, pupils in schools. mis_* are the missingness indicators, sch_manymiss a school flag; the remaining iq_perf/meetings/currmeet/mixedgra/sch_* are available covariates.

formula: joyread ~ female + age + immig + escs + (1 | school)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: Snijders & Bosker (2012) ch.14 survey-weights example (PISA, n=5233); the page names no response. Filed with reading enjoyment (joyread) as the student-level outcome, students in schools. w_fstuwt/w_fschwt are the PISA survey weights (ignored), stratum the sampling stratum (fixed design). metasum/undrem/private/urban/schsize/selsch/stratio remain as available covariates.

formula: laborinc ~ age + female + married + nrchildren + yearsed + emplstat + state + (age | id)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: Snijders & Bosker (2012) ch.15 longitudinal example (German SOEP, n=1236); the page names no response. Filed with labour income over age per person (id). totincbeforeg/totincafterg and healthsat/lifesat are alternate income/satisfaction outcomes, ob/birthyear/emplstat55 derived/redundant.

formula: langpost ~ ses + iq_verb + iq_perf + female + minority + (1 | school)
notes: Snijders & Bosker (2012) ch.16 multivariate multilevel model (Brandsma n=3773): language and arithmetic post-tests modelled jointly over schools; one registry row per response.

formula: aritpost ~ ses + iq_verb + iq_perf + female + minority + (1 | school)
notes: Snijders & Bosker (2012) ch.16 multivariate model, arithmetic response, row 2 (see model_index 1).

formula: relatt ~ edlevel + income + unemployed + relpar + female + single + divorced + widowed + gini + religiousregulation + tertiaryschoolenrollment + urbanization + (1 | country)
notes: Snijders & Bosker (2012) ch.17.1-17.5 discrete dependent variable: logistic multilevel model of religious attendance (relatt, dichotomous in the first rows) over individuals in countries, with individual- and country-level (gini, religiousregulation, ...) covariates. RULE GAP: relatt read as binary from the data; if it is a multi-category attendance scale the merge will flag it.

formula: scicourse ~ female + minority + ses + (1 | school)
notes: Snijders & Bosker (2012) ch.17.6-17.7 discrete dependent variable (Dekkers data, n=3432): whether a science course was taken (scicourse, logistic) and how many (scicount, count), students in schools; two responses -> two rows.

formula: scicount ~ female + minority + ses + (1 | school)
notes: Snijders & Bosker (2012) ch.17.6-17.7, count of science courses, row 2 (see model_index 1).

formula: cnt_mmb ~ female + age + isei + married + prtstnt + rural + (1 | regionnl)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: Snijders & Bosker (2012) ch.17.8-17.9 discrete dependent variable (Peter & Drobnic data, n=1738); the page names no response. Filed with cnt_mmb (a small count, 1-3) as the outcome over Dutch regions (regionnl). age_sqrd is age^2 (derived), idno the person id.

covariates: Normal score yr 1;Gender: boy=1;Social class: manual=1
formula: Normal score yr 3 ~ Normal score yr 1 + Gender + Social class + (1 | School ID)
notes: Goldstein, Multilevel Statistical Models (3rd ed., 2003), Junior School Project: year-3 attainment on year-1 attainment and background, pupils in schools. The normal (normalised) scores are the modelled variables; 'math yr 3'/'math yr 1' are the raw marks, ignored.

formula: Exam N-score ~ LRT N-score + gender + S class + (1 | Sec school)
notes: Goldstein (2003) JSP/exam data: exam normal score on London Reading Test score and background, pupils within secondary schools.

formula: written score, missing=-1 ~ gender + (1 | School)
notes: Goldstein (2003) multivariate GCSE example: written-paper and coursework scores modelled jointly over schools; one registry row per response. RULE GAP: the two score columns use -1 as a missing sentinel which the pandas reader does not convert to NaN, so the measured response will include -1 unless handled.

formula: coursework score, missing=-1 ~ gender + (1 | School)
notes: Goldstein (2003) multivariate GCSE, coursework response, row 2 (see model_index 1); missing=-1 sentinel as noted in row 1.

ignore: Biology core;Physics core;Biology form 3, missing=-1;Biology form 4, missing=-1;Physics form 2, missing=-1
formula: Environment science core ~ gender + (1 | School)
notes: Goldstein (2003) Hungarian science data: multivariate multilevel model of core-science exam marks (environment science, biology, physics) over students in schools; three core responses -> three rows, the optional form papers (Biology form 3/4, Physics form 2, missing=-1) left out and ignored. RULE GAP: marks are small integers (1-8); filed continuous (Goldstein's multivariate-normal fit) but could be ordinal.

ignore: Environment science core;Physics core;Biology form 3, missing=-1;Biology form 4, missing=-1;Physics form 2, missing=-1
formula: Biology core ~ gender + (1 | School)
notes: Goldstein (2003) Hungarian science multivariate model, response 'Biology core', row 2 (see model_index 1).

ignore: Environment science core;Biology core;Biology form 3, missing=-1;Biology form 4, missing=-1;Physics form 2, missing=-1
formula: Physics core ~ gender + (1 | School)
notes: Goldstein (2003) Hungarian science multivariate model, response 'Physics core', row 3 (see model_index 1).

covariates: Age centered about 13 years;Season, months from start of year
formula: Height (cm) ~ Age + Season + (Age | ID)
notes: Goldstein (2003) Oxford Boys growth data: height on centred age with a random slope per boy (ID); the classic polynomial-growth example (same data as nlme Oxboys and cmm_oxboys).

formula: Vote ~ 1 + (1 | Area)
notes: Goldstein (2003) British Election Study 1983: Conservative vote (binary) of voters within areas, an empty logistic random-intercept (variance-components) model.

formula: Contraceptive use ~ Number of children + Age + Urban + (1 | Area)
notes: Goldstein (2003) Bangladesh Fertility Survey: contraceptive use (binary) of women within areas, logistic multilevel model (same data as mlmRev Contraception and stata bangladesh).

covariates: Adult height, yes=1;Bone age response, yes=1;Age at height measure;Age at bone age measure
formula: Response ~ height/bone-age indicators + ages + (1 | Boy ID)
notes: Goldstein (2003) bivariate growth model of height and bone age, repeated measures per boy, in stacked MLwiN form: the single 'Response' column holds both height (cm) and bone-age values, the two indicator columns mark which, and the two age columns are the respective time axes. RULE GAP: a stacked multivariate response mixing two scales in one column.

formula: attitude to abortion ~ year + age (yr) + religion + (1 | Area) + (1 | respondent)
notes: Goldstein (2003) social-attitudes panel: abortion-approval score (0-7 count of circumstances) measured over four years per respondent, respondents nested in areas (same data as cmm_socatt).

formula: Height (cm) ~ nonlinear (Jenss-Bayley-type) growth curve in Age; individual-specific growth parameters
notes: NONLINEAR: Goldstein (2003) nonlinear growth-curve example, repeated height on age per individual, individual-specific nonlinear growth parameters.

formula: log duration ~ mother education + home + activity type + (1 | ID)
notes: Goldstein (2003) children's play-activity episodes per child (ID). RULE GAP: the book's model is a multinomial activity-choice model, but the activity type is stored as six one-hot dummy columns (activity 1-6) with no single categorical column, so the row is filed with log-duration (small integers) as the response and the activity dummies as covariates; episode is the within-child index.

formula: Exam score ~ VRQ score + (1 | Primary school) + (1 | Secondary school)
notes: Goldstein (2003) cross-classified model: pupils cross-classified by primary and secondary school, exam score on verbal-reasoning quotient. RULE GAP: Exam score is a 0-10 integer; filed continuous but could be a count/ordinal.

formula: change ~ episode + n_previous + social_class + start_age + (1 | id)
notes: Goldstein (2003) partnership repeated-events / discrete-time event-history data in person-period form: 'change' is the partnership-transition event, episode the time axis, n_previous and social_class covariates, id the person. 'partnership' (the current state) is the alternate response. RULE GAP: 'change' read as binary; if it codes transition type the merge will flag it. (goldstein_msm/partnership.txt is the same file read without a header, excluded.)

formula: weight ~ age + birthweight + gender + (age | child)
notes: Bristol CMM teaching data (Goldstein ML3-era): repeated weight measurements of Asian children over age, random growth per child.

formula: cbind(employed, total - employed) ~ gender + qualified + (1 | area)
notes: Bristol CMM teaching data: employed out of total in each gender x qualification cell within area, a grouped-binomial logistic model. cell is the within-area covariate-pattern id.

formula: score ~ vr1 + gender + fsm + vrband + ethnic + schgender + denomination + (1 | school)
notes: Bristol CMM teaching data (ILEA Junior School Project): exam score of pupils in schools on intake verbal-reasoning and background; vrband/ethnic/schgender/denomination are categorical codes. year is the cohort indicator (ignored).

formula: maths ~ year + gender + social + ravens + (1 | school) + (1 | school:class) + (1 | school:class:student)
notes: Bristol CMM teaching data (Junior School Project): maths and English over three years (year 0-2) per student, students within classes within schools. RULE GAP: a four-level nesting needing a three-part composite grouping (school:class:student) because student ids (1-3) repeat across classes; flag if the merge cannot build it. english/maths are the two responses.

formula: english ~ year + gender + social + ravens + (1 | school) + (1 | school:class) + (1 | school:class:student)
notes: Bristol CMM JSP, English response, row 2 (see model_index 1); same four-level structure.

formula: height ~ age + (age | student)
notes: Bristol CMM teaching data: Oxford Boys heights on centred age, random slope per boy (same data as nlme Oxboys and goldstein OXBOYS). occasion is the measurement index.

formula: written ~ gender + (1 | centre)
notes: Bristol CMM teaching data: GCSE science written and coursework scores modelled jointly over exam centres (schools); one row per response (same data as goldstein Gcsemv, here without the -1 missing sentinel).

formula: coursework ~ gender + (1 | centre)
notes: Bristol CMM GCSE science, coursework response, row 2 (see model_index 1).

formula: score ~ year + age + gender + class + party + religion + (1 | district) + (1 | respondent)
notes: Bristol CMM teaching data: social-attitudes-to-abortion score (0-7 count) over four years per respondent, respondents nested in districts (same data as goldstein SOCATT).
